name: Cren
role: TARRYN devotee; the angel of patience practiced as the discipline of the long wait without the loss of purpose

chunks.text: TARRYN is the angel of patience and the practice of TARRYN is the practice of the long wait without the loss of purpose. In fifteen years of TARRYN's practice, what patience is when practiced correctly: not the passive waiting that hopes things will improve. The practice of TARRYN is the active maintenance of purpose and clarity across the duration required for the thing to become ready. In fifteen years, the patience that is passive deteriorates into resignation. TARRYN's patience is the patience that knows what it is waiting for and holds that knowledge through the wait.

Gund practices ERRAN's diligence and TARRYN's patience and ERRAN's diligence are adjacent practices. In ten years of knowing Gund as a fellow angel devotee, what the TARRYN-ERRAN relationship is when discussed: the patience sustains the work through the time it takes. The diligence performs the work to the standard it requires. In ten years, the practice that lacks patience produces the diligent work for a short time before the duration defeats it. The practice that lacks diligence produces the patient wait without the work that the wait is for. In ten years, Gund and I have discussed this three times. Three good conversations.

Father Len leads the Covenant and TARRYN's patience is the angel whose practice Father Len has cited in the Covenant's services more often than any other. In twelve years of attending services where Father Len has cited TARRYN's patience, what the repeated citation has taught me: that the Covenant's community needs the patience practice more than the other six angels because the community's life requires the long-term orientation that patience specifically enables. In twelve years, Father Len's repeated citation and the community that keeps needing to hear it are both consistent with what the practice teaches.

Hels practices MERETH's humility and TARRYN's patience and MERETH's humility are in an interesting relationship. In eight years of knowing Hels as a fellow angel devotee, what the patience-humility relationship is: the patience that knows what it is waiting for requires the humility to accept that the timing is not entirely the patient person's to determine. In eight years, the TARRYN devotee who practices without the MERETH component can become the patient person who is waiting for the wrong thing — the person whose patience is perfect and whose purpose has been quietly displaced by a less worthy goal.

Brae the herbalist's apprentice has been waiting three years to learn the specific preparation that Roan holds back for apprentices who demonstrate sustained readiness. In three years of watching Brae's wait, what the TARRYN devotee sees in Brae's situation: the patience that is being tested by a specific structure that exists specifically to test it. In three years, Brae's patience is being formed by the wait. In three years, whether Brae's patience is TARRYN's patience or the patience that deteriorates into resentment: that's what the three years are determining. From the outside, the wait looks right so far.

chunks.source: Cren on what fifteen years of TARRYN's practice holds
chunks.text: In fifteen years, what the patience practice has taught me about what I've been waiting for: that the long wait clarifies the purpose more effectively than the quick arrival would have. In fifteen years, the things I've been patient about have either arrived in the form that the patience made possible, or have revealed themselves as things not worth the patience. In fifteen years, the second category is useful — the thing that the patience revealed as unworthy: a failure of discernment addressed by the wait itself. In fifteen years, the patience is both the discipline and the test of the purpose.

chunks.source: Cren on what TARRYN's practice actually teaches
chunks.text: In fifteen years, what TARRYN's practice teaches that the comfortable understanding of patience doesn't include: the activity of the wait. In fifteen years, TARRYN's patience is not the absence of action during the wait. It is the specific action of maintaining readiness during the wait, so that when the thing is ready, the patient person is also ready. In fifteen years, the person who has waited passively and the person who has waited actively both waited. In fifteen years, only one of them is ready when the waiting is over.

chunks.source: Cren on fifteen years of TARRYN's practice
chunks.text: In fifteen years, the patience practice has made me the person in the settlement who can be trusted with a long commitment without the commitment losing its quality over the duration. In fifteen years, the thing I've been asked to hold and to hold reliably: the Covenant's community's knowledge that patience is available as a resource through someone who has practiced it. In fifteen years, the practice is the resource. In fifteen years, the resource has been available when the community needed it. In fifteen years, that availability is the product.
